footer.disclaimer: Waterline is an educational tool built from published research on water-only fasting. It is not medical advice. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.

duration.short.name: Short fast
duration.shortterm.name: Short-term fast
duration.shortterm.note: 24 to 72 hours. Glycogen runs out and early ketosis begins.
duration.prolonged.name: Prolonged fast
duration.prolonged.note: 4 to 21 days of sustained ketosis. Research on fasts this long comes from supervised clinics with twice-daily checks and weekly blood tests.
duration.extreme.name: Extreme fast
duration.extreme.note: Over 21 days. Lean tissue loss, micronutrient depletion and heart strain become major concerns.
blocker.bmi.title: BMI of %@ (under 18.5)
blocker.bmi.why: Without enough fat and protein reserves, fasting can waste heart muscle and cause dangerous heart rhythms.
blocker.minor.title: Under 18
assess.warnings: Warning signs: %1$@. %2$@ If it feels severe, call your local emergency number.
assess.action.fast: End the fast and contact your clinician now.
assess.action.refeed: Contact your clinician now. These can be signs of refeeding syndrome or refeeding swelling.
assess.joint: A hot, swollen joint during a fast is often gout: ketones block uric acid clearance. An acute flare is a reason to end the fast.
assess.dizzy: Lightheadedness on standing is common on days 2 to 5 as blood volume drops. Get up slowly and rest. If you faint or nearly faint, stop the fast.
assess.sodium.likely: Cramps with headache, sluggishness or dizziness can point to low sodium (below 136 mmol/L). Only a blood test can tell. Let your clinician know.
assess.sodium.possible: Cramps or heavy drowsiness can be early signs of low sodium. Mention it to your clinician and keep watching.
assess.bp_drop: Blood pressure fell %1$lld/%2$lld mmHg when you stood up. A drop of 20/10 or more counts as orthostatic hypotension. Share it with your clinician and avoid sudden position changes.
assess.pulse_rise: Your pulse rose %lld beats a minute on standing, a sign of low blood volume.
assess.low_systolic: A lying systolic pressure of %lld mmHg is low. Rest and tell your clinician.
assess.bhb.high: BHB of %@ mmol/L is above the 3.0 to 7.0 range usually seen by days 5 to 10. Share the reading with your clinician.
assess.bhb.brain: BHB of %@ mmol/L: above 2.0, ketones are reaching the brain and covering much of its fuel.
assess.bhb.low: BHB of %@ mmol/L. Ketones start reaching the brain in quantity above 2.0 mmol/L.
assess.water.low: Yesterday you logged %@ L of water, under the 1.2 L minimum.
assess.water.high: Yesterday you logged %@ L of water, above the usual 1.2 to 2.5 L. Large amounts of plain water can lower blood sodium.
assess.weight_down: Down %1$@ kg (%2$@%%) since the start. Early loss is mostly water and glycogen, which come back when you eat.
assess.common: Common, mostly mild side effects. In 768 supervised fasts, 90% of people had at least one by day 5.
assess.none: No warning signs in this check-in.
kcal.low.headline: Start at 50 to 70% of your usual needs.
kcal.low.basis: Estimated from about %lld kcal a day for a restful day (Mifflin-St Jeor x 1.2).
kcal.low.missing: Add height, weight and age in Profile for a personal estimate.
kcal.moderate.headline: Start low, around 10 to 20 kcal per kg a day (the ASPEN starting range), and build up across 4 to 7 days.
kcal.high.headline: Limit to 5 to 10 kcal per kg a day and advance gradually, under medical care.
notify.h12.title: 12 hours in
notify.h12.body: Liver glycogen is running down and fat stores are opening up.
notify.h36.title: 36 hours: the metabolic switch
notify.h36.body: Ketone production is climbing. Get up slowly: lightheadedness on standing is common now.
notify.h72.title: The 72-hour threshold
notify.h72.body: Body-wide protein changes appear around now. Fasts beyond this point belong under medical supervision.
notify.d7.title: Day 7
notify.d7.body: Weight loss is slowing and the kidneys are saving sodium. Keep checking in twice a day.
notify.target.title: Target reached
notify.target.body: You reached your %@ target. End the fast in Waterline to get your refeeding plan.
notify.past_target.title: 12 hours past your target
notify.past_target.body: Your fast is still running. End it in Waterline to get your refeeding plan, or check in.
notify.unsupervised.title: 72 hours without supervision
notify.unsupervised.body: The research restricts fasts beyond 72 hours to medically supervised settings. End the fast now, or confirm in Waterline that a clinician is supervising.
notify.checkin.title: Time to check in
notify.checkin.body: Log lying and standing blood pressure, pulse, weight and how you feel.

stop.vomit: vomit and cannot keep water down

refeed_today.no_salt.title: No added salt yet.
refeed_today.no_salt.body: After a fast, insulin makes the kidneys hold on to sodium and water. Salt now can cause swelling and strain the heart.
refeed_warnings.title: Call your clinician if you notice
refeed_warnings.swelling: swelling in your ankles, legs or face
refeed_warnings.note: These can signal refeeding syndrome (phosphate, potassium and magnesium rushing into cells) or refeeding swelling (edema). Both are most likely in the first 3 to 5 days of eating again.

plan.doctor_reviewed: My doctor has reviewed this fast and my medicines.
plan.supervised: A clinician is supervising this fast, with regular checks of my blood pressure, pulse and blood tests.
plan.reason.bone: With osteopenia or osteoporosis, keep fasts to 72 hours or less.
plan.reason.long_needs_supervision: Fasts longer than 72 hours need a clinician supervising.
plan.reason.answers_need_supervision: Your answers mean this fast needs a clinician supervising.

before.title: Before you start
before.subtitle: What supervised clinics ask of people starting a fast.
before.doctor.title: See a doctor first
before.doctor.body: Blood tests (metabolic panel and blood count), a urine test and a resting ECG.
before.ease_in.title: Ease in for 48 hours
before.ease_in.body: Eat only raw and steamed fruit and vegetables for two days beforehand.
before.rest.title: Plan to rest
before.rest.body: Quiet walking and lying down only. Rest protects muscle and prevents fainting.
before.water.title: Drink 1.2 to 2.5 L of water a day
before.refeed.title: Block out time to refeed
before.refeed.body: At least half as long as the fast. A 10-day fast needs 5 days of careful refeeding.
teaser.title: What a water fast does, hour by hour
teaser.body: From the glycogen switch at 12 to 36 hours to the protein changes that appear around day 3, read what the research found, including the risks.
log.empty.title: No fast in progress
log.empty.body: Check-ins open once you start a fast. Each one records weight, blood pressure lying and standing, ketones and symptoms, then flags anything that needs attention.
checkin.title: Check in
checkin.optional: Fill in what you have. Every field is optional.
checkin.bp.title: Blood pressure and pulse
checkin.bp.how: Measure lying down after 5 minutes of rest, then after 1 to 3 minutes standing.
checkin.error.empty: Add at least one reading, symptom or note.
weight.title: Weight
weight.change_detail: kg change (%1$@%%), about %2$@ kg a day
weight.expected: Expected: 0.9 to 1.5 kg a day over the first 3 days, slowing to 0.25 to 0.40 kg a day by days 7 to 10. Across 5 to 20 day fasts about two-thirds of the loss is lean mass, mostly glycogen and water that return within 3 to 5 days of eating. The fat loss stays.
history.title: Past fasts
refeed.active.intro: After a fast of %1$lld hours, refeed for at least %2$@: half the length of the fast.
refeed.finish.title: Finished refeeding?
refeed.finish.body: Move on to a whole-food, low-sodium diet. Without lasting changes, blood pressure, blood sugar and blood fats drift back toward where they started within 3 to 4 months.
refeed.planner.title: Breaking a fast safely
refeed.planner.body: Coming off a fast is the riskiest part. Eating too much too fast can drive phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells all at once (refeeding syndrome), and salt can make the body hold fluid. Plan the way back before you start.
refeed.planner.prefilled: Prefilled with your current target. When you end the fast, this plan starts automatically.
refeed.planner.invalid: Enter a fast length between 1 and 40 days.
refeed.plan.needs_clinician.body: Significant-risk refeeding uses prescribed thiamine and daily blood tests.
refeed.plan.source: Ranges come from ASPEN and NICE refeeding guidance. Your clinician sets the final numbers.
refeed.plan.no_salt: Throughout: no added salt or salty seasonings. Insulin makes the kidneys hold sodium and water after a fast, which can cause swelling and strain the heart.
profile.summary.incomplete.body: Your answers decide which fasts Waterline will help you plan.
profile.summary.blocked.body: Talk to your doctor about what is safe.
profile.summary.clear: No red flags in your answers
profile.summary.clear.body: That does not replace a check-up. Clinics still run blood tests, a urine test and an ECG before a fast.

learn.title: What a water-only fast does to the body
learn.intro: Water-only fasting means no food and no caloric drinks, only plain water. With nothing coming in, the body runs on its own reserves, first glycogen and then fat turned into ketones. These changes can lower blood pressure and improve blood sugar markers. They also stress the kidneys, electrolytes and acid balance, which is why the research on fasts beyond a few days comes from medically supervised clinics.
learn.types.durations: Durations in studies: short-term 24 to 72 hours, prolonged 4 to 21 days, extreme over 21 days (up to 40 in some residential groups).
learn.hormones.title: Hormones and signals
learn.autophagy: Autophagy: once mTORC1 switches off, cells start breaking down and recycling damaged proteins and mitochondria. Fasting also raises spermidine, which keeps this recycling going.
learn.stat.early_loss: kg a day lost over days 1 to 3, mostly water and glycogen
learn.stat.later_loss: kg a day by days 7 to 10
learn.stat.lean_mass: of loss in 5 to 20 day fasts is lean mass, mostly regained within 3 to 5 days
learn.bp_why: Why blood pressure falls: low insulin makes the kidneys shed sodium and water. After 48 to 72 hours the nervous system calms (less sympathetic, more parasympathetic tone). BHB also relaxes artery walls through nitric oxide and potassium channels.
learn.benefits_fade: The benefits fade: 3 to 4 months later, blood pressure, glucose and blood fats are usually back near where they started unless eating habits change for good. A fast works as a short reset, not a cure.
learn.risks.intro: A review of 768 medically supervised water fasts (2 to 41 days, median 7) graded every side effect on the standard CTCAE scale.
learn.stat.any_effect: had at least one side effect by day 5, mostly mild
learn.stat.grade3: percent with a severe (Grade 3) event by days 5, 10 and 15
learn.stat.serious: life-threatening events / deaths, all under daily medical checks
learn.risks.common: Common mild effects: tiredness, nausea, poor sleep, headache, dizziness, fainting, indigestion, dry mouth and lower back pain.
learn.risks.electrolytes: Electrolytes: the body loses about 300 mEq of potassium over the first 7 days, even while blood levels look normal (3.5 to 4.0 mmol/L). Blood pH settles around 7.32 to 7.36 as bicarbonate is used up.
learn.refeeding.mechanism: During a long fast, the phosphate, magnesium and potassium stored inside cells run low, even when blood tests look normal. When carbohydrate returns, insulin drives these minerals into cells all at once. Blood phosphate can crash below 0.30 mmol/L (1.0 mg/dL). Without phosphate, red cells cannot release oxygen properly, which can lead to breathing failure, dangerous heart rhythms and muscle breakdown. Restarting carbohydrate also burns through thiamine (vitamin B1), risking lactic acidosis and Wernicke's encephalopathy.
learn.refeeding.edema: Refeeding swelling (edema) is a separate problem: insulin makes the kidneys hold sodium and water. Salt eaten too early can cause swollen legs, fluid on the lungs and heart strain.
learn.refeeding.aspen.title: ASPEN severity (drop in phosphorus, potassium or magnesium within 5 days of eating)
learn.refeeding.aspen.severe_value: Over 30%, or organ problems, or thiamine deficiency
learn.refeeding.higher_risk: Higher risk: little or no food for more than 7 to 10 days, BMI under 16, unintended loss of 10 to 15% of body weight in 3 to 6 months, or low phosphate or potassium before eating again.
learn.refeeding.rule: The rule of thumb: refeed for at least half as long as the fast, starting with diluted juice, then fruit and steamed vegetables, then starches and plant fats, with no added salt. The Refeed tab builds this plan for you.
learn.who.bmi: BMI under 18.5. Too few reserves to withstand starvation.
learn.who.relative: Needs a doctor and often inpatient care
learn.sources.note: Research papers are listed in the language they were published in.
phase.0.name: Running on your last meal
phase.0.text: Blood sugar comes from your last meal, then from glycogen stored in the liver. Insulin begins to fall.
phase.1.name: Glycogen runs down
phase.1.text: Liver glycogen is used up. Falling insulin unlocks fat stores, sending fatty acids and glycerol into the blood. Each gram of glycogen holds 3 to 4 g of water, so early weight loss is mostly water.
phase.2.name: The metabolic switch
phase.2.text: The liver turns the flood of fatty acids into ketones (acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate, or BHB). Low insulin makes the kidneys shed sodium, so blood pressure drops. Typical loss over the first 3 days is 0.9 to 1.5 kg a day, mostly water, glycogen and gut contents.
phase.3.name: The 72-hour threshold
phase.3.text: A study that tracked about 3,000 blood proteins daily saw only small changes for 48 hours. From the third day, about 36% of them changed together across every major organ system. 72-hour trials also show more autophagy markers (LC3-II, Beclin-1).
phase.4.name: Keto-adaptation
phase.4.text: Once BHB passes 2.0 mmol/L, ketones reach the brain and can cover 60 to 70% of its energy. The body needs less glucose made from muscle protein, so protein breakdown drops and steadies around days 4 to 7. The kidneys raise ammonium output to save sodium and potassium.
phase.5.name: Deep ketosis
phase.5.text: BHB usually sits between 3.0 and 7.0 mmol/L by days 5 to 10, up from under 0.1 mmol/L at baseline. IGF-1 falls 40 to 60% by days 5 to 8. Weight loss slows to about 0.25 to 0.40 kg a day as the kidneys switch to saving sodium.
phase.6.name: Prolonged fast
phase.6.text: Free T3 falls and metabolic rate drops to save energy. Under medical supervision, about 28% of fasters had a severe (Grade 3) side effect by day 10 and 32% by day 15.
phase.7.name: Extreme range
phase.7.text: Lean tissue loss, low micronutrients and strain on the heart become major concerns. Fasts this long have only been studied in residential medical settings.
risk.ortho.name: Low blood pressure on standing
risk.ortho.signs: Lightheaded, faint or a racing heart when you stand up.
risk.ortho.action: Sit on the edge of the bed before standing. Keep to rest and quiet walking.
risk.hypona.name: Low sodium (hyponatremia)
risk.hypona.action: Only a blood test can confirm sodium below 136 mmol/L. Tell your clinician. Stay inside your water target rather than drinking extra.
risk.acid.name: Ketone acid build-up (metabolic acidosis)
risk.acid.signs: Fast, deep breathing, nausea, extreme tiredness.
risk.acid.action: Fast, deep breathing means stop and get medical help.
risk.gout.name: High uric acid and gout
risk.gout.signs: Hot, red, painful swelling in a joint, often the big toe.
risk.gout.action: Keep up your water intake. An acute flare means ending the fast.
risk.bone.name: Bone mineral loss
risk.bone.signs: No symptoms. Shows up as more calcium in urine.
risk.bone.action: A reason to cap how long a fast runs, especially with low bone density.
screen.t1d.question: Type 1 diabetes
screen.t1d.why: Without your own insulin, a fast leads to diabetic ketoacidosis if insulin is stopped, or dangerously low blood sugar if it is not.
screen.preg.question: Pregnant or breastfeeding
screen.preg.why: A baby relies on a steady supply of glucose and amino acids, sustained ketones may affect brain development, and milk supply drops.
screen.ed.question: A current or past eating disorder (anorexia, bulimia, ARFID)
screen.ed.why: Stopping food can set off a serious relapse and carries a high risk of fatal refeeding problems. If eating feels hard right now, an eating disorder support service can help.
screen.ckd.question: Advanced kidney disease (CKD stage 3b to 5, or dialysis)
screen.ckd.why: The kidneys cannot clear the acid load, which risks severe acidosis and high potassium.
screen.liver.question: Cirrhosis of the liver with complications
screen.liver.why: The liver cannot store glycogen or make glucose well, so blood sugar stays dangerously low.
screen.porph.question: Acute porphyria
screen.porph.why: Cutting calories switches on the liver enzyme ALAS1, which sets off attacks.
screen.cachexia.question: Severe weight or muscle wasting (cachexia, sarcopenia)
screen.cachexia.why: Without fat and protein reserves, fasting can waste heart muscle and cause fatal heart rhythms.
screen.diuretic.question: Taking a diuretic (“water pill”)
screen.diuretic.why: Diuretics add to the sodium loss of fasting and can cause fluid collapse, fainting, low potassium and heart rhythm problems.
screen.diuretic.action: Your doctor has to stop it before the fast, and the fast needs inpatient monitoring.
screen.t2d.question: Type 2 diabetes treated with tablets or insulin
screen.t2d.why: Sulfonylureas cause severe low blood sugar without food. SGLT2 inhibitors can cause ketoacidosis even with normal glucose.
screen.t2d.action: Medicines must be tapered or stopped by a doctor, SGLT2 inhibitors well before the fast. Fast only under physician oversight.
screen.bpmeds.question: Taking blood pressure medicine (ACE inhibitor, ARB, calcium channel blocker, beta-blocker)
screen.bpmeds.why: Fasting lowers blood pressure by itself. Full doses on top can cause severe low pressure, fainting and poor blood flow to the kidneys.
screen.bpmeds.action: Only your doctor should reduce or stop these.
screen.lithium.question: Taking lithium or another psychiatric medicine with a narrow safe range
screen.lithium.why: Dehydration and sodium changes slow lithium clearance and raise the risk of toxicity.
screen.lithium.action: Needs close monitoring by your prescriber.
screen.gout.question: Gout or high uric acid
screen.gout.why: Ketones compete with uric acid for removal by the kidneys, which can set off a gout flare.
screen.gout.action: Drink enough water and have uric acid checked during the fast.
screen.bone.question: Osteopenia or osteoporosis
screen.bone.why: Long fasts draw minerals from bone to buffer ketone acids.
screen.bone.action: Fasts over 72 hours are off the table. Keep any fast short.
screen.heart.question: Heart disease or a heart rhythm problem
screen.heart.why: Electrolyte losses can trigger rhythm problems, and refeeding can overload the heart with salt and fluid.
screen.wtloss.question: Lost more than 10% of your body weight without trying in the last 3 to 6 months
screen.lytes.question: Been told you have low phosphate, potassium or magnesium
stage.juice.title: Diluted juice
stage.juice.text: Fresh fruit or vegetable juice diluted with water, 100 to 200 mL every 2 to 3 hours. It gently restarts stomach acid, digestive enzymes and insulin.
stage.fruitVeg.title: Whole fruit and steamed vegetables
stage.fruitVeg.text: Raw whole fruit and steamed non-starchy vegetables, in small meals.
stage.starch.title: Add starches and plant fats
stage.starch.text: Complex carbohydrates such as sweet potato or brown rice, plus modest plant fats like avocado, nuts or seeds. Keep avoiding concentrated animal fats and refined sugar.
tier.low.label: Lower risk
tier.low.criteria: Fast under 5 days, normal electrolytes and a healthy BMI.
tier.low.fluids: Drink to thirst. Keep added salt out at first, then bring it back slowly.
tier.low.monitoring: Baseline checks only. Get tested if symptoms appear.
tier.moderate.label: Moderate risk
tier.moderate.criteria: Fast of 5 to 7 days, or BMI 16 to 18.5.
tier.moderate.fluids: No added salt. Make sure food supplies potassium and phosphorus.
tier.moderate.monitoring: Vital signs twice a day and blood electrolytes every 48 hours.
tier.high.label: Significant risk
tier.high.criteria: Fast over 7 days, BMI under 16, recent unintended weight loss over 10%, or low electrolytes before refeeding.
tier.high.fluids: Thiamine (vitamin B1), 100 to 300 mg a day as prescribed. No added salt. Electrolytes replaced as needed.
tier.high.monitoring: Daily blood tests (electrolytes, magnesium, phosphorus) for 3 to 5 days.
protocol.water.name: Water-only
protocol.water.allowed: Plain distilled or mineral water, 1.2 to 2.5 L a day or more
protocol.water.setting: Residential, with twice-daily checks and lab tests
protocol.buchinger.name: Buchinger
protocol.buchinger.allowed: Vegetable broth, fresh juice, herbal tea with honey
protocol.buchinger.setting: Residential or outpatient, run by certified therapists
protocol.fmd.name: Fasting-mimicking diet
protocol.fmd.allowed: Plant-based soups, energy bars, teas, a glycerol drink
protocol.adf.name: Alternate-day fasting
protocol.adf.calories: 0 kcal or a small allowance on fast days
protocol.tre.name: Time-restricted eating
protocol.tre.allowed: Water and zero-calorie drinks while fasting
hormone.insulin.why: No carbohydrate or protein coming in
hormone.insulin.effect: Unlocks fat stores; kidneys shed sodium
hormone.bhb.effect: Main brain fuel; relaxes blood vessels
hormone.gh.why: Response to falling insulin and glucose
hormone.igf1.why: Liver stops responding to growth hormone
hormone.igf1.effect: Halts cell growth signals; more stress resistance
hormone.ft3.why: Less thyroid hormone activated in the liver
hormone.mtor.why: Amino acids run low; AMPK switched on
hormone.uric.why: Ketones block its removal in the kidney
study.goldhamer.cohort: 174 adults with high blood pressure, water fast averaging 10.5 days
study.goldhamer.finding: 89% reached a reading under 140/90 mmHg. People starting above 180/110 dropped 37/13 mmHg on average. Everyone on blood pressure medicine stopped it during the fast with no rebound.
study.dai.cohort: Overweight men without diabetes, 10-day water fast
study.dai.finding: Weight fell 7.28 kg (9.8%). Systolic pressure was down 6.44% by day 7 and 14.68% at its lowest, on the first day of refeeding. Sodium, chloride and IGF-1 fell.
study.oglodek.finding: Lower blood pressure, weight, BMI, fat-free mass and body water. Low sodium (under 136 mmol/L) developed, and uric acid clearance fell.
study.pietzner.finding: Average loss of 5.7 kg, with the lean mass regained after refeeding. A distinct change in blood proteins appeared from day 3, involving about 36% of those measured.
study.scharf.cohort: Adults with obesity, no diabetes, 17-day water fast
study.scharf.finding: Body weight fell 10.2%. Blood pressure, fasting glucose, insulin and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) fell. Triglycerides rose for a while.
complication.sodium.name: Low sodium
complication.sodium.cause: Sodium loss from low insulin, plus plain water
complication.sodium.signs: Cramps, sluggishness, headache, dizziness on standing
complication.sodium.response: Watch fluid intake; sometimes oral salt
complication.gout.name: High uric acid, gout
complication.gout.cause: Ketones compete with urate in the kidney
complication.gout.signs: Red, painful, swollen joint, often the big toe
complication.gout.response: Keep hydrated; end the fast for an acute flare
complication.ortho.name: Low blood pressure on standing
complication.ortho.cause: Lower blood volume and a calmer nervous system
complication.ortho.signs: Near-fainting, lightheadedness, racing pulse on standing
complication.ortho.response: Strict rest; slow position changes; vital signs
complication.acid.name: Metabolic acidosis
complication.acid.signs: Fast, deep breathing, nausea, extreme tiredness
complication.acid.response: Track bicarbonate; start refeeding if blood pH falls
complication.bone.name: Bone mineral loss
complication.bone.cause: Bone releases calcium salts to buffer acid
complication.bone.response: Cap fast length; avoid long fasts with low bone density
